task.name: Environment Protection Drift Remediation
task.description: Review the GitHub production environment in a covered repository and surface only protection-rule settings that differ from the repository's approved production-environment policy, excluding branch protection, workflow token permissions, deployment manifests, and runtime deployment configuration.
task.intent: Reduce operator time spent discovering and correcting drift in production environment approval, wait-timer, and deployment-branch or tag restrictions without duplicating findings that are already tracked or explicitly accepted.
activationConditions: A scheduled review occurs or a repository environment-policy or production-environment protection-rule change is observed within the evidence window.
Authoritative repository environment evidence shows at least one production environment protection-rule setting differs materially from the approved production-environment policy.
requiredEffects: Each novel finding identifies the production environment, the drifted protection-rule setting, its approved value, its observed value, and repository-linked evidence supporting the comparison.
Maintainers can accept, reject, or resolve each surfaced finding using repository-linked environment, policy, and audit evidence.
noopConditions: The production environment's required reviewers, wait timer, and deployment branch or tag restrictions match the approved production-environment policy.
Every supported environment-protection drift finding is already tracked or covered by an unexpired, explicitly accepted exception.
successConditions: Supported environment-protection drift findings receive accepted remediation evidence or an explicit maintainer dismissal within 14 days of the workflow run.
In-policy environment settings and drift covered by an accepted exception create no duplicate maintainer attention.
uncertainties: GitHub plan, repository visibility, or environment configuration can make some protection-rule fields unavailable, which must produce missing attainment rather than inferred compliance.
A temporary production change may be authorized outside the policy file but remains drift until repository-linked exception evidence identifies its scope and expiry.

operationalValue.statement: The proportion of supported, novel production environment-protection drift findings assigned to the run that are restored to policy or explicitly dismissed within 14 days.
operationalValue.opportunity: One workflow run and the deduplicated supported protection-rule drift findings it assigns for the repository's production environment.
acceptedEvidence: Repository environment and audit evidence showing the identified required-reviewer, wait-timer, or deployment branch or tag restriction now matches the approved production-environment policy before the evidence cutoff.

A closed tracking issue, pull request conversation, or repository-linked exception record that explicitly marks the finding resolved, dismissed, or intentionally accepted by a maintainer and identifies any exception expiry.
evidenceRepositories: The repository in which the workflow ran and whose production environment and approved policy were evaluated.

metric.name: resolved-supported-environment-protection-drift-findings
metric.formula: restored-to-policy-or-dismissed supported environment-protection drift findings / supported novel environment-protection drift findings assigned to the run

operationalValue.maturation: 14 days after the workflow run completes.
operationalValue.zeroRule: Return 0 when at least one supported novel environment-protection drift finding was assigned and none has accepted resolution evidence by the evidence cutoff.
operationalValue.missingRule: Return null when the assigned finding set, approved production-environment policy, or required repository environment or audit evidence cannot be read.

rows.finding-summary: Production requires two reviewers but currently has one; no unexpired exception is recorded.

rows.outcome-summary: Repository environment evidence records two required reviewers matching policy.
